title: Choose the landing page structure
question: The colours, type and crop marks stay. Pick how the page is built: which arrangement tells a print shop what Sylvi does.

options.label: Trimmer passes
options.thesis: The page is one sheet cut apart in passes; every section is a strip.
options.viewport: A tall 2x2-height strip holds the headline beside four prints; a magenta cut runs edge to edge under it, then a shorter 1x1 strip.
options.risk: Strip heights follow print sizes, so long copy has to fit the rhythm, not the other way round.

raised.raise: Strips pack edge to edge with no gap between them, the way Sylvi packs a sheet.

options.label: The sheet is the page
options.thesis: The whole landing page is one sheet lying on the mat, laid out like a Sylvi layout.
options.viewport: A ruler along the top, one sheet with a mat border; the hero is the big cell, two 2x2 prints beside it, three short cells below.
options.risk: A page inside a frame loses width on small laptops; the margin has to shrink hard on phones.

options.label: One job, start to finish
options.thesis: Follow a single walk-in order on its job slip, from Messenger photo to cut prints.
options.viewport: Headline on the mat at left; Bea's job order slip at right with her photo clipped on, stages ticking as you scroll.
options.risk: One customer's story can hide that Sylvi handles many sizes and shared sheets; later sections must widen it.

options.label: Now serving board
options.thesis: A shop's queue board: one row per customer, flipping to Ready as Sylvi finishes their sheet.
options.viewport: Headline over a full-width board of five customers with number, order, paper and status; rows flip as they're served.
options.case: Fuses well: Filipinos know Now serving boards from NBI and PSA offices; loses narrowly on showing the sheet itself.
options.risk: Shows the queue more than the photos, so the sheet must appear right below the board.
